newsitem.title: ITALY: Data shows Italy inflation heading for 28-year low.
newsitem.headline: Data shows Italy inflation heading for 28-year low.

text.p: Italian inflation is set to fall to a 28-year low this month, according to preliminary data released on Tuesday, boosting hopes of a swift cut in the official discount rate.
Consumer inflation should drop to 1.7 percent year-on-year in April against 2.2 percent in March, analysts said after 11 Italian cities released their monthly price data.
The last time inflation reached such a low level in Italy was April 1969. That was also the last time the consumer price index held beneath the two percent threshold.
Since then Italian inflation has been on a freewheeling roller-coaster ride, peaking at 21.1 percent in 1980, before being gradually tamed over the last decade.

Inflation stood at 4.5 percent in April 1996 and has fallen steadily over the past 12 months as Prime Minister Romano Prodi's centre-left government put the fight against price rises at the centre of its economic policy.
The CPI slowdown has been rewarded by the Bank of Italy with three cuts to the discount rate over the last 10 months, each time by 75 basis points, to the current 6.75 percent.

Treasury undersecretary Roberto Pinza said on Tuesday he hoped further monetary easing was in the pipeline. "Certainly the violent fall in the inflation rate makes one hope for something from interest rates," he told reporters.
The hope was echoed by industrialists and union leaders alike and was reflected in the market, with many analysts expecting an imminent rate cut.

"With CPI under 1.8 percent, the Bank of Italy has to cut," said Martino Dofini at Chase in Milan. "With a cut the lira would appreciate and this would be a signal that the central bank is confident that things are going well," he added.
Sharda Persaud with San Paolo Bank in London expected a cut later on Tuesday of 50 basis points. "A cut of 50 basis points is quite small and will not be a risk for the lira," she said.
However other analysts argued for caution, with the lira looking unsteady and European markets jittery in the wake of France's decision to hold a snap general election next month.
The lira was trading at 995.7 to the German mark at 1535 GMT, against a central parity rate in the European exchange rate mechanism (ERM) of 990.
"At this level of exchange it is dangerous to cut rates," said Gianluca Sanna, an economist with analysts' group Stone & McCarthy in London.

But the government will be anxious for Bank of Italy action as it battles to reduce its huge debt servicing costs. Prodi has estimated that the treasury saves some 20 trillion lire ($11.8 billion) a year for every percentage point fall in rates.

Treasury Minister Carlo Azeglio Ciampi said on Tuesday that the fall in inflation opened the way for a pick-up in the sluggish economy. "It lays the basis for a recovery in production," Ciampi said in a statement.
He added that the government had worked to overhaul state accounts and bring stability to its monetary policy.
"There will be no fears of inflation rising, even with the expected increase in demand," he said. $1 = 1,700 lire
